_README: Ground truth about fields the agent keeps misreading when it turns a JSON
payload into a document. This is a FIXTURE, not configuration: every entry
should come from an observed failure, and should say what the wrong reading
looks like so the checker can recognise it.
Why this file exists (docs/todo.md item 2a): across two runs the agent
transcribed 239 of 240 table cells correctly and still produced a wrong
document, because it selected the wrong FIELD. Every digit of the bad value
was copied faithfully from the source, so a source-to-document diff cannot
catch it. Field meaning is not recoverable from the payload; it has to be
Matching is per-source, keyed on a substring of the fetched URL, so a field
called 'duty' on some other device is never judged by this entry.
raw_register  the value is a hardware register, not a human-facing metric
inverted      max_value means OFF (a BC547 low-side switch, here)
prefer        the field that actually answers what the raw one looks like
unit          declared unit; used to sanity-check derived spans
stale_when_cached  value is a live counter, meaningless from cache

duty.note: PWM register after a BC547 inversion: 255 is OFF, 0 is full power. Reported as 'Duty Cycle: 252' in two separate documents, which reads as near-full power and is actually about 1%.

dp.note: The real power figure. This is what 'duty cycle' should report.

s.note: Seconds of uptime, not a timestamp, and the payload carries no unit. A 40-point history spans (40-1)*30 = 1170 s = 19.5 min. One run reasoned its way to '7.5 days' from these numbers.

uptime.note: A running counter. Two fetches 4.5 minutes apart both reported 91 s because the second was served from cache (item 17).

t2.note: Second sensor. Absent entirely from the 31e0af64 document.
